source_review.notes: Checked the Karger consistent-hashing paper, Dynamo paper, jump consistent hash paper, and original rendezvous report; checked current official Cassandra, Redis Cluster, PostgreSQL, Spanner, DynamoDB, and Ceph documentation. All twelve referenced URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed the key domain, canonicalization, partition function, logical unit, ownership epoch, replica placement, range-boundary, fixed-hash, token-ring, churn, balance, and full design-tuple notation.
Checked half-open endpoint semantics, wraparound selection, denominator conditions, and separation of versioned logical assignment from physical placement.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation distinguishes keys, logical ranges or buckets, primary owners, replicas, map versions, workload weights, and evidence.

evidence: Executed partition-movement-comparison with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced modulo movement 8,917/10,000, jump movement 1,135/10,000, and explicit range-split movement 1,250/10,000.
Recomputed nine-bucket load vectors, boundary lookups 6200->r2 and 6800->r4, exercise maximum-to-mean 700/250=2.8, and the ideal new-destination share 1/9.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All fixture counts are exact for the declared finite keys and functions; expected consistent-hash shares remain probabilistic, not universal guarantees.

evidence: Re-derived range membership from strictly ordered half-open boundaries and checked unique assignment at each boundary.
Derived why direct modulo couples assignment to the divisor and why stable slots preserve the hash-to-slot function when physical membership changes.
Checked the ideal equal-capacity consistent-mapping argument that a new destination receives approximately 1/(n+1) of the key space in expectation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Movement, balance, replication, availability, and migration correctness are kept as separate claims.

evidence: Reviewed exact range endpoints, unbounded sentinels, null and invalid keys, monotonic keys, popular prefixes, low cardinality, large values, hot keys, collisions, inconsistent serialization, integer-width differences, and arbitrary membership removal.

Reviewed stale routers, redirect loops, dual-write partial success, missed deletes, reordered retries, source rejoin, replica co-location, rebalance overload, split-merge oscillation, rollback, offline medical devices, and degraded networks.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial key distributions and transition failures are evaluated separately from uniform finite fixtures.

evidence: Traced canonicalization, total single-valued assignment, range coverage, exclusivity, stable bucket identity, epoch-compatible routing, distinct replica placement, and one authoritative owner through exposition and exercises.
Checked that hot-key lower bounds, weighted churn, transfer capacity, rollback evidence, and source retirement conditions are explicit.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not infer replication, topology safety, or authority transfer from a partition function alone.

evidence: Reviewed all eight selection and transition obligations from key contract through retained evidence.

Checked counterexamples for balanced ranges, hash-equals-balance, modulo scale-out, zero-movement consistency, token-equals-node, next-token replicas, free hash tags, copy-only validation, and dual-write safety.
Reviewed range split identity and the staged copy, catch-up, validation, cutover, drain, recovery, and retirement argument.
proof_review.notes: Steady-state mapping correctness, probabilistic distribution quality, and online transition safety are treated as distinct proof obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of correct, proof, expected, ideal, stable, safe, authoritative, balanced, direct, and minimal.
Confirmed the 1/(n+1) statement is labeled as an ideal equal-capacity expectation and fixture movement is labeled as finite observation.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No deterministic algorithm or local result is presented as a universal distribution, availability, or migration guarantee.

evidence: Reviewed current-system examples, retrieval dates, executable output, fixture scope, non-benchmark disclaimer, and production validation requirements.
Confirmed no production, clinical-safety, certification, performance, availability, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Real selection requires retained workload distributions, exact implementation conformance, target-system fault tests, and consequence-appropriate review.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed range, fixed hash, ring consistency, virtual nodes, slots, rendezvous, jump, directory placement, composite keys, churn, balance, replication, and epoch transition as one coherent selection model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed portable hash contracts, boundary indexes, hot-key diagnosis, topology-aware replica choice, membership caching, capacity-weighted movement, online transfer states, reconciliation, rollback, observability, and source retirement. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from ordered ranges through hashing and low-churn mappings to migration; ten worked examples and five complete answers cover retrieval, calculation, comparison, design, and unfamiliar clinical transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, large-scale data practitioner, database vendor, clinical, safety, or certification review is claimed.
